newsitem.title: USA: UAW engine plant workers approve contract.
newsitem.headline: UAW engine plant workers approve contract.

text.p: Striking workers at a Chrysler Corp. engine plant approved a new contract Friday despite criticism from opponents of the pact, ending a month-long strike against the nation's No. 3 automaker.

The vote by employees of the company's Mound Road Engine plant in Detroit was 1,009 for and 182 against. The walkout had disrupted production of some of Chrysler's most profitable vehicles -- full-sized pickups and sport utility vehicles.

Chrysler said machining division and drive-shaft division workers at Mound Road were expected to start returning to work on Saturday. More than 18,000 workers at other plants idled by the strike were expected to be back on the job by Tuesday.
Analysts have estimated the strike will end up costing Chrysler as much as $475 million.

United Auto Workers leaders told union members at the ratifcation meeting Friday that production of drive shafts will remain at the plant, a different interpretation of the agreement from Chrysler and some industry analysts. The union had said farming out the work could have cost up to 300 jobs.
"Chrysler did not win. The story has been distorted," said John Guinan, a member of the UAW's international bargaining committee.
Leaders of UAW Local 51 said the drive shaft work will be phased out over a two-year period. The plant will be upgraded, and the work brought back in by 2001 or 2002.
But some Local 51 members expressed anger over shifting work to outside suppliers, shouting at union officers in a smoke-filled cafeteria where the meeting was held.
"You don't start a job and not finish it," said Mike Langsdale, a 25-year veteran at the plant.
While he applauded the drive shaft agreement, Langsdale said the new contract does not force Chrysler to stop its current practice of shifting production of some engine parts away from the plant.

Langsdale also criticised union leaders for not discussing the fine print of the contract until hundreds of members had cast their ballots. "They showed the shiny side of the penny before the voting," he said.

Chrysler agreed to invest $75 million in the plant and install a new engine block production line. Mound Road workers also will have the option of transferring to Chrysler's new Mack Avenue Engine plant in Detroit that will start volume production in mid-1998 for the 1999 model year.

Union leaders warned they will still have to deal with the issue of shifting work to outside suppliers at the Mack Avenue plant. Those will be addressed in a separate bargaining agreement. Chrysler expects to hire 600 to 1,000 workers for the plant, the union said.

Meanwhile, General Motors Corp. continued talks to resolve strikes at two of its assembly plants. About 3,500 hourly workers are on strike at the company's plant in Oklahoma City that assembles Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass models.
More than 5,800 UAW members are also on strike against GM's pickup truck plantin Pontiac, Mich.
Chrysler stock rose 75 cents to $31.25 and GM added $1.125 to $57.875, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
